slot.brief: Bayes' theorem word problem: given prior probabilities and conditional probabilities, find the posterior probability of a cause.

stem: Machines $A,B,C$ are used with probabilities $\frac12,\frac13,\frac16$. Two checks are conditionally independent given the machine; their pass probabilities are $(\frac12,\frac12)$ for $A$, $(\frac23,\frac34)$ for $B$, and $(\frac34,p)$ for $C$. If both checks pass with probability $\frac{17}{48}$, find the probability the item came from $C$, given both checks passed.

verdicts.working: By total probability, \(\frac18+\frac16+\frac p8=\frac{17}{48}\), so \(p=\frac12\). Thus \(P(C\mid\text{both pass})=\frac{(1/6)(3/4)(1/2)}{17/48}=\frac3{17}\).

working:
$$\frac12\cdot\frac14+\frac13\cdot\frac12+\frac16\cdot\frac34p=\frac{17}{48}\quad\Rightarrow\quad p=\frac12$$
$$P(C\mid\text{both pass})=\frac{\frac16\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac12}{\frac{17}{48}}=\frac{3}{17}$$

Independent check: By total probability, \(\frac18+\frac16+\frac p8=\frac{17}{48}\), so \(p=\frac12\). Thus \(P(C\mid\text{both pass})=\frac{(1/6)(3/4)(1/2)}{17/48}=\frac3{17}\).
solution:
By conditional independence and total probability,
$$\frac12\cdot\frac14+\frac13\cdot\frac12+\frac16\cdot\frac34p=\frac{17}{48},\qquad p=\frac12.$$
Hence, by Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(C\mid\text{both pass})=\frac{(1/6)(3/4)(1/2)}{17/48}=\frac{3}{17}.$$
